pr.title: Avoid MIR bloat in inlining
pr.description:
In #126578 we ended up with more binary size increases than expected.

This change attempts to avoid inlining large things into small things, to avoid that kind of increase, in cases when top-down inlining will still be able to do that inlining later.

processing.reason: The PR (#127113) changes only the MIR `Inline` pass's size/cost heuristic: it lowers the threshold for `#[inline]` forwarder callers (30 vs 100), adds a `CALL_PENALTY` bonus for callees with exactly one call-like terminator, and adjusts library inlining attributes. It does not change any dataflow, value computation, borrow, drop, or evaluation-order semantics. Inlining a callee or leaving the call in place produces the same observable behavior; the regression tests added by the PR are MIR-shape/dump expectations (`CHECK: call_twice`, `CHECK-NOT: other_thing`, presence/absence of inlined scopes), not runtime value checks. The supplied analysis explicitly notes this is "a size/MIR-bloat heuristic, not a semantic bug fix" and that tests "should assert on MIR shape ... not runtime behavior." Therefore there is no source-grounded original-vs-incorrect pair that yields different defined numeric/boolean/character results under Miri. Constructing a pair that diverges at runtime would require inventing an unrelated semantic rewrite, which the task forbids.

analysis.summary: MIR `Inline` heuristic change: avoid inlining large callees into small `#[inline]` forwarding callers by giving such callers a lower (default 30) threshold, and give a function-level bonus to callees whose body contains exactly one call-like block. This targets binary-size/MIR-bloat regressions from earlier inlining behavior.
analysis.originalLogic: Before the patch, `check_mir_body` selected the inlining threshold solely from cross-crate inlinability: `let mut threshold = if cross_crate_inlinable { ... inline_mir_hint_threshold.unwrap_or(100) } else { ... inline_mir_threshold.unwrap_or(50) };`. There was no notion of the caller being a simple `#[inline]` forwarder, and `CostChecker` had no function-level bonus for callees containing exactly one call-like terminator (`add_function_level_costs` did not exist). Consequently, a callee up to the hint threshold (default 100) could be inlined into a tiny `#[inline]` function that only forwards to it.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Historically, the `Inline` pass could inline a relatively large callee (cost above the forwarder threshold of 30 but within the hint threshold of 100) into a caller that is itself a small `#[inline]` forwarding function, i.e. a caller whose START_BLOCK terminator is a `Call`, whose optional target block terminates in `Return`, and whose remaining blocks only contain `Return`/`Drop`/`UnwindResume`/`UnwindTerminate`. The corrected transformation detects `caller_is_inline_forwarder` and applies `inline_mir_forwarder_threshold.unwrap_or(30)` instead, keeping the forwarding call rather than duplicating the large callee body into the forwarder. Separately, a callee with exactly one `Call`/`Drop`/`Assert`/`InlineAsm` terminator now gets a `CALL_PENALTY` bonus because inlining it does not increase the total number of calls.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR inlining decisions in `compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/inline.rs` / `cost_checker.rs`, at `-O` (with `-Zinline-mir` enabled), for callers whose `codegen_fn_attrs.inline` is `InlineAttr::Hint` or `InlineAttr::Always` and whose body matches the small-forwarder shape. The differentiating callee has inlining cost above 30 but at or below the normal hint threshold (default 100), e.g. a function containing two call-like blocks such as two calls to an extern function. A non-`#[inline]` caller and a callee with a single call-like block are control cases.
analysis.trigger: Triggered while the `Inline` pass evaluates a callsite: `caller_is_inline_forwarder` is true when the caller has `InlineAttr::Hint | InlineAttr::Always` and `body_is_forwarder(body)` is true, selecting the forwarder threshold (default 30). Independently, `add_function_level_costs` adds `CALL_PENALTY` to the bonus whenever the callee body has exactly one call-like terminator.
preconditions: Caller must carry `#[inline]` (Hint or Always); a plain non-inline caller does not use the forwarder threshold.
Caller body must start with a `Call` terminator; if that call has a target, the target block must terminate in `Return`.
Caller body block count must be within the forwarder limits: 2 for non-polymorphic bodies, 3 for polymorphic bodies with no call target, otherwise 4.
Every non-START block must terminate only in `Return`, `Drop`, `UnwindResume`, or `UnwindTerminate`, so functions with additional calls/branches are not classified as forwarders.
For the function-level bonus, the callee body must contain exactly one block whose terminator is `Call`, `Drop`, `Assert`, or `InlineAsm`.
pitfalls: Do not conflate forwarder classification with ordinary inline-hint behavior: the order of checks matters, and the forwarder branch takes precedence over the `cross_crate_inlinable` hint branch.
`body_is_forwarder` allows only a restricted terminator set and block-count limits; a body that also has an `Assert`, `SwitchInt`, `Goto`, or extra call is not a forwarder.
The single-call-like bonus counts `Drop`, `Assert`, and `InlineAsm` as call-like, not just `Call`; `Goto`, `SwitchInt`, `UnwindResume`, `UnwindTerminate`, `Return`, and `Unreachable` are not counted.

This is a size/MIR-bloat heuristic, not a semantic bug fix. Changing it does not alter program semantics, only whether inlining occurs; tests should assert on MIR shape (presence/absence of inlined scopes and calls), not runtime behavior.

The patch compensates in library code by adding `#[inline]` markers and splitting `RawVec::shrink` into an inlined check plus `shrink_unchecked`, because reducing forwarder inlining can otherwise hurt codegen/inlining outcomes.

The MIR test expectations changed for `slice_iter` and `inline_shims` precisely because large inner bodies are no longer inlined into forwarders; do not interpret those deletions as evidence of a wrong replacement pass.
analysis.testStrategy: Add MIR-opt regression tests under `tests/mir-opt/inline/` compiled with `-O --crate-type lib` and `// EMIT_MIR_FOR_EACH_PANIC_STRATEGY`. Define an `#[inline]` callee that performs two calls (`call_twice`), then three callers differing only in caller shape/attributes: (1) a non-`#[inline]` caller, which should still inline `call_twice` and show both `other_thing` calls; (2) an `#[inline]` direct forwarder calling `call_twice`, which should NOT inline it (`CHECK: call_twice`, `CHECK-NOT: other_thing`); (3) an `#[inline]` forwarder calling the second forwarder, which may inline the forwarder (single call-like bonus) but should still keep `call_twice` uninlined. Use `// EMIT_MIR` and `CHECK-LABEL`/`CHECK-NOT` to pin MIR output for both panic strategies. Also use `-Zinline-mir-forwarder-threshold` to vary the boundary, and `-Zinline-mir-hint-threshold` to verify the forwarder threshold takes precedence. For the single-call bonus, compare callees with one vs. two call-like terminators at a fixed threshold. Do not rely on executing the compiler; these are MIR-dump expectations.
